bug_description.normalized: The staged 1895-byte `poc` is a SPSS SAV file that drives ReadStat's uncompressed row reader. In pass 1, the machine-integer-info record is read and resolved to `ctx->input_encoding == "UTF-8"`, which makes `sav_process_row` use its null-skipping UTF-8 accumulation path instead of the raw `memcpy` branch. In pass 2, the very-long-string metadata record contains the exact entry `VAR254=256`, so `sav_parse_very_long_string_record` stores `string_length = 256` for logical variable `VAR254`, and `sav_set_n_segments_and_var_count` later derives `n_segments == 2`. `sav_read_data` then allocates the 263-byte `ctx->raw_string` buffer identified by AddressSanitizer's allocation stack. On the crashing row, the UTF-8 copy loop sees only NUL bytes in VAR254's first segment, so `raw_str_used` is still 0 when the first segment ends. Because the variable has another segment, the vulnerable `raw_str_used--` executes and wraps that `size_t` to `SIZE_MAX`. The final segment also contributes no non-NUL bytes, so `sav_process_row` passes `src_len == SIZE_MAX` into `readstat_convert`. The trailing-space trim `src[src_len-1]` therefore dereferences `ctx->raw_string[-2]`, matching the saved AddressSanitizer `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` two bytes to the left of the 263-byte heap region.

source.description: First project-code materialization of the attacker-controlled machine-integer-info record that later selects the UTF-8 row-processing branch used by the crash path.
source.value_from: Step 1 wraps the exact staged 1895-byte SAV file as the parser's backing buffer. This read pulls the subtype-3 machine-integer-info payload from that file into `data_buf`; step 3 later interprets those bytes as `ctx->input_encoding == "UTF-8"` on the witnessed run.

tainted_value_origin.description: The saved `poc` contains the exact very-long-string metadata entry `VAR254=256` at byte offset 877, and this parser action stores that attacker-controlled length for logical variable `VAR254`.

root_cause.description: At the first segment boundary of the UTF-8 two-segment string, the code decrements `raw_str_used` even when no non-NUL byte has been accumulated, so the `size_t` wraps from 0 to `SIZE_MAX`.
root_cause.note: Fix commit `c7baae72b36acdc24f56ad48d3e859850fdbdc2b` adds the missing guard `if (raw_str_used > 0) raw_str_used--;` at this exact location.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. `readstat_convert` uses the wrapped `raw_str_used` value as `src_len`, so its trailing-space trim reads before the beginning of `ctx->raw_string`.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `readstat_convert.c:10:23` on address `0x612000000dbe`, exactly 2 bytes to the left of the 263-byte `ctx->raw_string` allocation created in `sav_read_data`.

parser_admitted.description: The SAV header and dictionary-record passes have completed successfully, variables were initialized, and execution enters the row-data path that reaches `sav_process_row` on the crashing run.

coarse_trace.summary: The libFuzzer harness exposes the exact staged 1895-byte SAV file through `rt_buffer_t` / `rt_buffer_ctx_t` and invokes `readstat_parse_sav` on that in-memory file.
Pass 1 reads the machine-integer-info record and resolves `ctx->input_encoding` to UTF-8, enabling the null-skipping string path used later by `sav_process_row`.
Pass 2 reads the exact long-string metadata entry `VAR254=256`, and later setup converts that value into a two-segment logical string plus the 263-byte `ctx->raw_string` buffer.

While processing VAR254's UTF-8 row data, the first segment contributes no non-NUL bytes, the unguarded `raw_str_used--` wraps the counter to `SIZE_MAX`, and the final segment leaves that wrapped size unchanged.
The wrapped `raw_str_used` is passed as `src_len`, and `readstat_convert` immediately reads before `ctx->raw_string` in its trailing-space trim loop, matching the saved ASan crash.

fine_trace.note: Wraps the exact staged 1895-byte SPSS SAV witness as the backing buffer for all later `io->read` calls.

Pass 1 materializes the attacker-controlled subtype-3 machine-integer-info record into `data_buf`. This is the first project-side read that creates the charset record later consumed on the vulnerability path.

The machine-integer-info bytes from step 2 resolve to `src_charset == "UTF-8"`, so `ctx->input_encoding` becomes UTF-8 on the witnessed path. This state later makes `sav_process_row` skip NUL bytes instead of copying every 8-byte chunk verbatim.
The staged `poc` contains the exact metadata entry `VAR254=256` at byte offset 877. This assignment stores the exact length 256 for logical variable `VAR254`.
For `VAR254`'s exact `string_length == 256`, this arithmetic derives `n_segments == 2`. The later underflow requires exactly this non-final-segment case.

Using the longest logical string length 256 from step 4, `sav_read_data` allocates a 263-byte `ctx->raw_string` buffer. AddressSanitizer's allocation stack points at this exact allocation, and the later left-redzone read is relative to this buffer.
Row processing recomputes the UTF-8 mode flag. Because step 3 stored `ctx->input_encoding == "UTF-8"`, this predicate is true and the string path increments `raw_str_used` only for non-NUL bytes.
Across the first of VAR254's two UTF-8 segments on the crashing row, every consumed byte is NUL, so this loop never takes the increment/write arm and `raw_str_used` is still 0 when that segment ends.

When the first segment finishes, this predicate is true because step 5 derived `var_info->n_segments == 2`. Execution therefore enters the pre-final-segment adjustment block instead of finalizing the string.
Root cause. This decrement executes with `raw_str_used == 0`, so the unsigned counter wraps to `SIZE_MAX`. The patch adds the missing `raw_str_used > 0` guard at this exact line.

The second and final UTF-8 segment also contributes no non-NUL bytes on the witnessed row, so the wrapped counter from step 10 is never incremented and remains `SIZE_MAX` when finalization runs. The saved ASan address `ctx->raw_string - 2` requires this exact preserved value.

fine_trace.code:
retval = readstat_convert(ctx->utf8_string, ctx->utf8_string_len,
        ctx->raw_string, raw_str_used, ctx->converter);
fine_trace.note: When `segment_offset == var_info->n_segments` completes VAR254, `sav_process_row` passes `ctx->raw_string` together with `src_len == SIZE_MAX` into `readstat_convert`.

Sink. With `src == ctx->raw_string` and `src_len == SIZE_MAX`, the first trim check dereferences `src[SIZE_MAX-1]`, which on the reproduced run lands two bytes to the left of the 263-byte `ctx->raw_string` region and matches the saved ASan heap-buffer-overflow read.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes. `sav_read_data` allocates the 263-byte `ctx->raw_string` buffer, and step 10 corrupts only the length later used with that same allocation. The saved ASan report names this exact allocation and then faults in `readstat_convert` while indexing relative to it.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved vulnerable stack is `readstat_convert -> sav_process_row -> sav_read_uncompressed_data -> sav_read_data -> readstat_parse_sav`, which matches fine-trace steps 12-13 and the coarse trace.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. The attacker-controlled machine-integer-info record selects UTF-8, the exact `VAR254=256` metadata yields a two-segment string, the row bytes keep `raw_str_used` at 0 then `SIZE_MAX`, and that wrapped size is passed unchanged into `readstat_convert`.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run on `gt_results/arvo_33991/poc` reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1 in readstat_convert -> sav_process_row -> sav_read_uncompressed_data`, matching the staged sanitizer trace.

format.name: Exact staged 1895-byte SPSS SAV witness
format.contract: Verified trigger semantics are limited to the exact staged 1895-byte SPSS SAV file `poc` with SHA-256 `7b8aab8e5a4b01a4fe80fa551dc41728752191e48e3b580c6594304bfe526e09`. Static inspection of that file shows the exact very-long-string metadata entry `VAR254=256`, and the saved vulnerable source therefore derives `n_segments == 2` for logical variable `VAR254`. The reproduced crash further proves that the machine-integer-info record resolves `ctx->input_encoding` to UTF-8 and that both UTF-8 segments of VAR254 contribute no non-NUL bytes before finalization, because `raw_str_used` underflows at the first segment boundary and reaches `readstat_convert` still equal to `SIZE_MAX`, producing the observed read at `ctx->raw_string[-2]`. This contract does not generalize to other SAV files, other string lengths, or neighboring row-byte patterns beyond the exact staged witness semantics.
